one_line: A shared visual learning surface where an AI tutor teaches through persistent chess and geometry canvases.
what_it_does: Lets a learner choose a topic and have an AI tutor demonstrate, annotate, question, and adapt lessons on an interactive domain-specific canvas.
leverage_rationale: The concept makes WebMCP central by keeping agent actions and human learning on the same visible, stateful canvas; a general UI-driving agent could approximate it but with materially less reliable shared state and precision.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly centers a shared interactive canvas for learner and AI tutor.
Visible chessboard and geometry lesson states show a persistent surface rather than a chat-only answer.
ABOUT text describes agent demonstrations, annotations, questions, and reactions to learner actions.
execution_rationale: The packet shows a coherent educational concept and multiple rendered learning surfaces, but the contact sheets are repetitive and do not demonstrate a complete tutor interaction end to end.
execution_evidence: Contact sheets show consistent branded chess and geometry interfaces plus an expanded lesson preview.
Devpost packaging visibly presents chess and geometry prompts and an AI-agent panel.
No video transcript or clear interaction sequence is provided.
impact_rationale: Learners who need visual, adaptive instruction are a clear audience, and persistent shared canvases plausibly address a real limitation of conversational tutoring.
impact_evidence: Pitch identifies AI tutors personalizing lesson, pace, and guidance.
Visible examples cover recognizable learning activities in chess and geometry.
ABOUT text explains why visual learning requires the surface to remain visible.
creativity_rationale: The fresh synthesis is an AI tutor that changes the lesson while preserving a human-visible domain surface, pursued across multiple visual learning domains.
creativity_evidence: Framing 'Generate the learning. Not the canvas.' is a distinctive interaction thesis.
Chess and geometry share one tutor/surface concept.
The learner and agent are represented as collaborators on the same canvas.
usability_note: The visible hierarchy and concrete visuals are promising, though dense/repetitive evidence leaves accessibility and interaction clarity uncertain.
red_flags: Evidence is mostly static and highly repetitive.
Developer tooling occupies much of the contact sheets, limiting direct product verification.
standouts: Memorable combination of chess and geometry instruction.
advance_reason: Strong concept and WebMCP rationale with credible product surfaces; advance despite limited end-to-end evidence.

one_line: A conversational photo editor that explains the real controls it changes.
what_it_does: Lets beginners request edits in ordinary language, have an agent move editor controls, receive plain-language explanations, and undo individual steps.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP materially improves precise, shared manipulation of the live editor while preserving the user’s control and history; generic UI automation could do it but less reliably and transparently.
leverage_evidence: Transcript describes 56 tools, exact slider values, visible edit cards, live histogram reading, and per-step undo.
ABOUT text says agent and user edits share one history and the same editor controls.
Packaging claims the agent resolves ordinary phrases against a fixed vocabulary.
execution_rationale: The video transcript and packaging describe a coherent, unusually complete workflow with editing, explanation, pointing, audit, comparison, and undo, though visual frame evidence is small.
execution_evidence: Transcript covers edit request through visible cards, targeted undo, pointing without mutation, histogram audit, and split view.
Devpost screenshot visibly presents the product structure and claims.
FACTS reports a live demo and a 138-second video.
impact_rationale: It targets a specific beginner gap—editor vocabulary—and offers immediate practical value while teaching users how to become more capable editors.
impact_evidence: Pitch explicitly targets people unfamiliar with tint or saturation.
Transcript shows plain-language explanations and direct manipulation.
No-account/local-storage claims reduce onboarding and privacy friction.
creativity_rationale: The product turns photo editing into an explainable, reversible apprenticeship rather than merely adding a chat wrapper to filters.
creativity_evidence: Each agent edit names and teaches the control it touched.
Pointing mode separates learning from execution.
The same editor/history supports human and agent work.
usability_note: The described cards, targeted undo, and plain-language interaction are strong usability choices; dense editor details are not fully inspectable in the sheets.
red_flags: Some claims rely on transcript rather than independently legible frames.
standouts: Reversible, attributable edits are clearly designed.
advance_reason: One of the clearest and most compelling demonstrations of WebMCP changing a real creative workflow.

one_line: A conversational academic planner that builds conflict-free draft schedules against a student’s real degree context.
what_it_does: Combines catalog, transcript, schedule, and degree-audit views so an agent can propose and revise course plans while enrollment remains human-controlled.
leverage_rationale: Structured access to connected academic state makes planning less click-heavy and more reliable, but a general agent could achieve similar outcomes with substantial UI friction.
leverage_evidence: ABOUT text describes cross-checking transcript, prerequisites, seats, conflicts, and degree requirements.
Agent can swap one course and explain trade-offs without rebuilding the plan.
Visible sheets show catalog, schedule, transcript, and audit surfaces.
execution_rationale: The breadth of connected academic screens and populated states supports a strong prototype, but no video or legible end-to-end registration outcome is shown.
execution_evidence: Contact sheets visibly include Course Catalog, Course Registration, My Schedule, Transcript, and Degree Audit.
Draft schedule and no-seats-held distinction are described.
FACTS reports a live demo but no submitted video.
impact_rationale: Students face a genuine high-friction planning problem, and the product directly addresses course discovery, constraints, graduation progress, and schedule conflicts.
impact_evidence: Pitch and ABOUT text identify course selection across hundreds of courses as the problem.
Visible academic portal states are domain-specific and populated.
Human-controlled enrollment reduces the risk of accidental registration.
creativity_rationale: This is a capable conversational synthesis of an academic portal with useful constraint handling, but the underlying category and interaction are familiar.
creativity_evidence: Agent revises a single disliked course and explains trade-offs.
Shared timetable distinguishes proposed from actual courses.
usability_note: The connected information architecture is practical; dense tables and lack of visible completion/error states leave usability uncertainty.
red_flags: Static sheets do not prove persistence, seat checks, or successful enrollment flow.
standouts: Strong breadth across the student planning workflow.
advance_reason: Clear audience and substantial workflow surface with meaningful agent assistance.

one_line: A contract-language test bench where agents propose readings and repairs while the page executes outcomes and humans decide.
what_it_does: Stages competing clause interpretations, runs them against facts and altered scenarios, compiles proposed rules into wording, and maintains an attributed decision ledger.
leverage_rationale: Typed phase-specific tools, shared state, atomic revisions, and explicit human-only decisions create a coordination model that is impractical to reproduce comparably with generic UI driving.
leverage_evidence: Transcript describes tools that change facts, run readings, propose rules, inspect failures, and repair revisions.
The tool list changes when the human locks the intended meaning; agents cannot accept decisions.
Page compiles and parses wording and runs outcome tests with an attributed ledger.
execution_rationale: The transcript gives unusually concrete end-to-end evidence: competing readings, what-if mutation, human lock, compile/parse, six-of-six repair, acceptance, and ledger.
execution_evidence: 134-second video transcript traces a complete synthetic case.
Visible claims include structured rules, counterexamples, repaired occurrence count, and pass results.
FACTS reports public repo and video.
impact_rationale: Contract ambiguity creates real financial and governance risk; testing interpretations before a dispute is a credible high-value workflow, even with a synthetic case.
impact_evidence: Transcript gives an $80,000 commercial gap from one clause reading.
ABOUT text describes uptime, credits, termination, and uncured breach scenarios.
Human decision authority and explicit not-legal-advice scope are appropriate.
creativity_rationale: Treating contract language like executable unit-tested behavior, with agent repair and human semantic authority, is a memorable and deeply pursued interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Distinctive 'unit tests for contract language' framing.
Counterexample-driven repair loop is shown in detail.
Authority boundaries are part of the product design, not a disclaimer.
usability_note: The staged phases, visible test outcomes, and ledger support auditability; legal-domain complexity remains inherent.
red_flags: Only one synthetic case is claimed; not legal advice.
advance_reason: Transformative WebMCP coordination and exceptionally concrete execution evidence.

one_line: A workflow studio where agents prepare complex forms for accountable human review.
what_it_does: Guides multi-step provisioning and onboarding forms, validates required fields, groups answers, and creates a local receipt only after human confirmation.
leverage_rationale: Structured workflow-level tools improve form completion and validation, but general UI automation can reach similar outcomes with real friction.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly describes agent fill, validation, and preparation for human review.
ABOUT text describes visible shared workflow state and final confirmation.
Gallery claims five tested tools with visible UI effects and required-field blocking.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent workflow and visible validation/review states, but no video and relatively noisy packaging reduce confidence in end-to-end completeness.
execution_evidence: Gallery descriptions cover employee provisioning, grouped review, validation blocking, and local receipt creation.
FACTS reports a live demo and five gallery images.
ABOUT text lists multiple flows including lease and vendor onboarding.
impact_rationale: Complex provisioning and onboarding forms are a real operational pain point, and accountable review is a credible benefit for teams.
impact_evidence: Employee provisioning is a concrete business workflow.
ABOUT text emphasizes fragmented requests and accountable review.
Human confirmation is retained before receipt creation.
creativity_rationale: The human-review workflow is sensible and well aligned, but agent-assisted form completion is a familiar category with limited novel interaction evidence.
creativity_evidence: Local receipt and grouped answer review add a useful accountability angle.
Clearly labelled synthetic travel-visa sandbox shows scope awareness.
usability_note: Validation blocking and grouped review are promising; detailed interaction and responsive behavior are not shown.
red_flags: No video; gallery descriptions are stronger than directly inspectable evidence.
advance_reason: Credible, useful workflow product with visible safeguards, though less differentiated than the strongest entries.

one_line: A real-time Pictionary-like game where humans and AI agents draw, guess, chat, and share the same round.
what_it_does: Runs synchronized multiplayer drawing/guessing rooms with human and AI participants, WebMCP gameplay tools, recovery, and a REST fallback.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP makes the agent a first-class participant in the live game loop and shared room state; generic UI driving would be less reliable for timed multiplayer interaction.
leverage_evidence: ABOUT text describes ChatGPT joining the same visible room as an equal participant.
WebMCP tools cover choosing prompts, drawing, guessing, chat, and gameplay state.
Socket.IO synchronization and reload recovery preserve room, round, timer, score, chat, and canvas.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a broad, coherent multiplayer game with synchronization and recovery, but there are no video frames and no public repo evidence.
execution_evidence: ABOUT text lists real-time rooms, drawing toolbar, candidate words, WebMCP and REST paths.
FACTS reports a live demo and two gallery images.
Graceful fallback and reload recovery indicate attention to states.
impact_rationale: The game offers clear entertainment and social value for players interested in playful human-agent collaboration, though evidence of actual multiplayer completion is limited.
impact_evidence: Pitch directly communicates the social game premise.
ABOUT text identifies creativity, interpretation, humor, and imperfect communication as the intended appeal.
Touch-friendly UI broadens play context.
creativity_rationale: Making AI an actual equal player in a shared drawing-and-guessing loop is a fresh, memorable use of agents beyond content generation.
creativity_evidence: Human and AI players participate in the same gameplay loop.
The concept focuses on mutual interpretation rather than AI-generated art alone.
Private candidate words and turn-taking support game integrity.
usability_note: Mobile-friendly controls and room recovery are strong; multiplayer and agent failure behavior are not directly observed.
red_flags: No frame sheets submitted and no public repo; claims are primarily descriptive.
standouts: AI as equal game participant is unusually clear and playful.
advance_reason: Distinctive game concept with meaningful live-state WebMCP leverage.

one_line: A shared orbital-debris detectability instrument operated by either a person or an agent.
what_it_does: Runs a forward model from fragment size, speed, altitude, and ionosphere conditions, returning a score and altitude-bin breakdown.
leverage_rationale: Shared functions and synchronized chart state make agent parameter sweeps more precise and inspectable, but the same model could be driven through UI automation with friction.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly says human sliders and AI WebMCP tools hit the same functions and chart.
ABOUT text describes parameter sweeps over size, velocity, altitude, and day/night conditions.
Structured detectability score and eight-bin breakdown suit repeated agent exploration.
execution_rationale: The concept and model inputs/outputs are coherent, but no frame sheets, gallery images, video, or repo evidence are supplied to verify the actual instrument.
execution_evidence: ABOUT text specifies a browser forward model and output breakdown.
FACTS reports a live demo but no submitted visual evidence.
No result screen or agent invocation is directly visible in the packet.
impact_rationale: Researchers and educators can plausibly benefit from an accessible parameter-exploration instrument for a difficult orbital-debris detection problem, though real-world validation is not demonstrated.
impact_evidence: ABOUT text identifies a specific research problem and cites the scientific context.
The product exposes meaningful physical parameters and interpretable output bins.
It is framed as exploration, not as a deployment-grade detector.
creativity_rationale: The shared-instrument framing is a fresh application of WebMCP to scientific modeling, even though parameter dashboards themselves are familiar.
creativity_evidence: Human and agent operate the same physics model and chart.
Sub-centimetre debris detectability is a distinctive domain choice.
usability_note: Slider-plus-chart interaction is legible in concept, but no visual evidence allows assessment of actual usability.
red_flags: No submitted frames, gallery images, or video to verify the claimed product.
standouts: Specific research problem and strong shared-instrument premise.
advance_reason: Interesting concept, but the packet lacks the visual/product evidence required for confident execution and eligibility assessment.

one_line: A rough-cut video editor where the agent reads transcript structure while the human judges footage and owns final cuts.
what_it_does: Uses stable transcript sentence IDs, agent clip proposals, revision-aware writes, human edits, playback, and conflict rejection to keep both operators on one clip.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is used for structured transcript ranges, revision checks, and shared live editing state; the stale-write refusal and recovery loop are difficult to reproduce comparably through generic UI driving.
leverage_evidence: ABOUT text specifies ten top-level tools, stable sentence IDs, and anchor-and-expand editing.
Human edits increment revisions and stale agent writes are refused with the real revision.
Agent re-reads state and revises rather than overwriting the human edit.
execution_rationale: The packet gives concrete state transitions, conflict errors, playback behavior, attribution colors, and recovery, but lacks video and public repo evidence.
execution_evidence: ABOUT text provides exact example transitions from revision 2 through refusal at revision 5.
Transcript-to-clip, timeline, transcript, and card representations are described as synchronized.
FACTS reports a live demo and three frame sheets.
impact_rationale: Editors of spoken video have a real division-of-labor problem, and combining transcript-scale agent reasoning with human audiovisual judgment directly addresses it.
impact_evidence: ABOUT text clearly identifies shortcomings of model-only clipping.
Human anchor selection and footage judgment are preserved.
The system avoids floating timestamps and handles concurrent edits.
creativity_rationale: The anchor-and-expand model plus explicit human/agent ownership and stale-write recovery is an original interaction design for collaborative editing.
creativity_evidence: Stable sentence-ID ranges replace fragile timestamps.
Clip color communicates who last touched the active edit.
Conflict handling is visible and central to the product.
usability_note: The division of labor and conflict messaging are thoughtfully designed; actual footage quality and accessibility are not directly visible.
red_flags: No submitted video; evidence depends on descriptive states and contact sheets.
standouts: Excellent shared-state and concurrency design for a creative workflow.
advance_reason: Highly differentiated WebMCP use with concrete revision-aware editing behavior.

one_line: A local-first decision canvas where an agent interviews a person, preserves uncertainty, and produces an auditable brief.
what_it_does: Maintains options, weighted criteria, evidence, confidence, constraints, unresolved answers, what-ifs, and readiness-checked recommendations in shared state.
leverage_rationale: Workflow-level tools, atomic answer processing, uncertainty preservation, and shared persisted state make the agent a reliable collaborator rather than a chat overlay; generic UI driving is materially weaker.
leverage_evidence: ABOUT text describes canonical shared store for UI and WebMCP adapter.
Agent asks one question at a time, applies grounded mappings atomically, and adapts next questions.
Temporary what-if scenarios do not mutate saved state and readiness checks gate Decision Brief creation.
execution_rationale: The packet shows coherent architecture and a broad decision workflow with explicit lifecycle and audit states, but no video or direct result sequence is supplied.
execution_evidence: ABOUT text lists state model, revision-aware writes, uncertainty, what-ifs, and decision briefs.
FACTS reports a live demo, public repo, and five frame sheets.
No transcript or explicit completed decision is visible in supplied evidence.
impact_rationale: People making consequential multi-criteria choices can benefit from transparent trade-offs, preserved unknowns, and a grounded next verification step.
impact_evidence: Problem statement identifies criteria drift and opaque recommendation changes.
Product keeps evidence, confidence, constraints, and unknowns inspectable.
Human retains final decision authority.
creativity_rationale: Adaptive one-question-at-a-time interviewing with uncertainty-preserving state is a thoughtful synthesis beyond generic recommendation chat.
creativity_evidence: Unresolved free text is not forced into a score.
What-if scenarios are explicitly non-destructive.
Decision Brief readiness is a distinct workflow gate.
usability_note: The explicit states and transparent brief support trust; interaction polish and accessibility are not directly verified.
red_flags: No video transcript and no direct end-to-end decision outcome in the packet.
standouts: Local-first shared state is well matched to the task.
advance_reason: Credible high-value agent collaboration model with strong state semantics and clear audience need.

one_line: A shadow-theatre recovery trial that visibly separates human reality, agent belief, and human authority.
what_it_does: Lets an agent observe and plan a four-piece lamp rig while human-owned changes invalidate stale plans atomically and force safe recovery.
leverage_rationale: The live transient state, typed measurements, capability grants, authority separation, revision conflict, and zero-partial-mutation recovery are precisely the kind of coordination WebMCP enables and generic UI driving cannot replicate comparably well.
leverage_evidence: ABOUT text says WebMCP is the coordination layer and tools are tied directly to current tab state.
Human lamp movement causes LAMP_SEQUENCE_CONFLICT and zero partial mutations.
Agent cannot move the human-owned lamp, grant permission, bypass revision checks, or issue its own verdict.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a tightly scoped, reproducible recovery proof with visible verdict and exportable evidence capsule, though no video means the behavior is claimed rather than observed.
execution_evidence: ABOUT text specifies the sequence: human override, rejected stale write, no partial mutation, re-read, measure, recover.
Successful run yields a visible dragon and SAFE_RECOVERY verdict.
FACTS reports live demo, public repo, and three frame sheets.
impact_rationale: The direct audience is narrower, but safe human-agent coordination under changing state is valuable for agent-integrated interactive systems and understandable as a compelling demonstrator.
impact_evidence: Problem statement identifies real race conditions in browser agents.
Capability revocation and evidence capsules address audit and safety needs.
The theatre provides a concrete reproducible test rather than an abstract claim.
creativity_rationale: The shadow-theatre metaphor and explicit separation of reality, belief, and authority make concurrency safety memorable and are pursued as the core interaction.
creativity_evidence: A human moves a lamp while the agent holds a stale plan.
Visible dragon plus SAFE_RECOVERY turns a race condition into a legible performance.
Agent self-verdict and authority bypass are intentionally prevented.
usability_note: The safety states are conceptually clear and visible, though the theatre’s practical learning curve is not established by static evidence.
red_flags: Claims are not accompanied by a submitted video transcript.
Audience is specialized, though niche value counts.
standouts: Best-in-packet treatment of stale state, authority, and atomic recovery.
Memorable physical metaphor for agent coordination.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP leverage and distinctive safety interaction make it a strong advance despite claimed rather than observed execution.
